about: The polish cases of the three answers at every permission point (fix-j33-three-answers, 2026-11-15), in the shape of polish.json: one per point's text. Where an index would make the question fast (the world link index) the answer offers it with its size, build time and later time; where none would, it says so. In a file of their own so that other fixes' cases don't collide with them. They expect no world link index in the test home (the world index of every plugin with world data); case 134 makes and drops one of kgcdoom.esm only.

cases.title: refs: world data left out by default offers world true and world "save_index", each with its cost (fix-j33-three-answers)
cases.before: The line said only "Add world: true (command line: --world) to include it: about 4 s more"; nothing said that an index would answer it in a fraction of a second.

pass_if.name: run now with its time, save the world link index with its size, build time and later time, or leave it out

all.matches: (?m)^World data wasn't searched \(left out by default: more than 256 MB of it\): [\d,]+ records .* Add world: true \(command line: --world\) to include it: about \d+ s more

(?m)^Or world: "save_index" \(command line: --world=save-index\) to search it now and then save the world link index of [\d,]+ plugins \(about [\d,.]+ (MB|GB) on disk, made in about \d+ s in the background after the answer\): refs into world data then answers in about 0\.2 s, from the index\. Or leave it out, as this answer did\.$

cases.title: refs: world true searched by its bytes says what world "save_index" would save next time (fix-j33-three-answers)
cases.before: Nothing said that the seconds of a world byte search could be a fraction of a second with the world link index.

pass_if.name: the note names the bytes searched and the third answer with its cost

all.matches: by its bytes: [\d,]+ records of [\d,]+ plugins

World data was searched by its bytes \([\d.]+ GB in [\d,]+ plugins\)\. To make this fast next time, call with world: "save_index" \(command line: --world=save-index\) to search it the same way and then save the world link index of [\d,]+ plugins \(about [\d,.]+ (MB|GB) on disk, made in about \d+ s

cases.title: query2: world types left out of Links WHERE ToKey offer the world link index (fix-j33-three-answers)

params.sql: SELECT FromType, count(*) AS N FROM Links WHERE ToKey = '003321:Starfield.esm' GROUP BY FromType;

pass_if.name: the types left out, how to read one, and allow_heavy="save_index" with the index's cost

all.matches: Not read for Links, because each is over the cost limit by itself: [^\n]*PlacedObject \([\d,]+ records\)[^\n]* Or allow_heavy="save_index" \(command line: --allow-heavy=save-index\) to get this answer as it is and then save the world link index of [\d,]+ plugins \(about [\d,.]+ (MB|GB) on disk, made in about \d+ s in the background after the answer\): Links WHERE ToKey = '…' then finds the world records that link to a record in about 0\.1 s and reads only those

SELECT FromType, Field, count(*) AS N FROM Links WHERE ToKey = '003321:Starfield.esm' AND FromType = 'PlacedObject' GROUP BY Field;

pass_if.name: run now (time and memory), save the index (size, build time, later time), leave it; the JSON's saveIndex

all.matches: (?m)^Not run\. PlacedObject in [\d,]+ plugins is [\d,]+ records .*: about \d+ s and about [\d.]+ GB to read.* Call again with allow_heavy=true \(command line: --allow-heavy\) to run it now\. Or allow_heavy="save_index" \(command line: --allow-heavy=save-index\) to run it now and then save the world link index of [\d,]+ plugins \(about [\d,.]+ (MB|GB) on disk, made in about \d+ s in the background after the answer\): .* Or leave it: nothing more is read and nothing is saved\.$

SELECT EditorID, Json FROM Cell LIMIT 2;

cases.title: sources2: a plugin of over 300,000 placed references without a world link index is searched by its bytes by default, says so and offers the index; the answer is allow_heavy's (fix-j63-scope-reads, GAPS S100; was fix-j33-three-answers, GAPS S96)
cases.before: "Starfield.esm has more than 300,000 placed references (…): they weren't searched for placed copies, so an item placed in it isn't listed as one. Call again with allow_heavy=true …" (the three answers; by default they were left out).

pass_if.name: searched by its bytes by default, how long it took, save the world link index of Starfield.esm next time; the same answer as allow_heavy

all.matches: Starfield\.esm has more than 300,000 placed references \([\d,]+, [\d.]+ MB\) and no world link index: their bytes were searched for placed copies with the other plugins' \([\d,]+ pass(es)? over [\d,]+ placed references, [\d.]+ s\)\. To make this faster next time, call again with allow_heavy=\"save_index\" \(command line: --allow-heavy=save-index\) to search them the same way and then save the world link index of Starfield\.esm \(about [\d,]+ MB on disk, made in about \d+ s in the background after the answer\): placed copies of an item then come from it in a fraction of a second
